citation: Centofanti S, et al. 2024. Fasting as an intervention to alter the impact of simulated night-shift work on glucose metabolism in healthy adults: a cluster randomised controlled trial. Diabetologia 68:203.
protocol: Baseline sleep 8 h in bed, 4 nights of simulated night shift (7 h sleep opportunity 10:00-17:00) then 1 recovery sleep; 75 g glucose drink after overnight fast with samples at -15, 0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150 min (OGTT), plus a standard breakfast test
population: n=55 healthy adults without obesity (age 24.5 +/- 4.8 y, BMI 24.8 +/- 2.8 kg/m2), three arms

reports.where: Table 2 (fasting and OGTT indices), Table 3 (postprandial glucose after breakfast test, means and SEM)
Table 2 (fasting and OGTT indices), Table 3 (postprandial insulin)

note: Table 2 (OGTT indices) and Table 3 (breakfast-test curves) carry glucose and insulin; Table 1 and 2 headers say mean +/- SD, Table 3 says mean and SEM, so the uncertainty flag is mixed. Three arms (fasting, snack, meal at night) on simulated night shift; the sleep opportunity is 7 h in the daytime.
